context: State dp[i, j] is the minimum number of edits to change the first i characters of s into the first j characters of t. Insertion, deletion, and replacement each cost 1. For s = book and t = code (current prefix lengths i = 4, j = 4), the diagram shows the possible predecessors when the final characters s[i-1] = k and t[j-1] = e differ.
description: The current state dp[i, j] is on the left. Three branches on the right show insertion (addition), deletion, and replacement from top to bottom. Grayed-out final characters have matched or been deleted and are outside the remaining prefixes.

After insertion, the new character matches the target's last character. No original source character is consumed, so only j decreases by 1. Deletion removes only the last source character, so only i decreases by 1. After replacement, the last characters match and both i and j decrease by 1.

For each branch in order, the table distinguishes the source string after editing from the remaining source prefix and gives the corresponding subproblem state. The diagram does not calculate the final edit distance from book to code.

frames.explanation: Each operation costs 1 edit. Choose the one whose remaining subproblem requires the fewest edits. For unequal final characters, dp[i,j] = min(dp[i,j-1], dp[i-1,j], dp[i-1,j-1]) + 1.
frames.title: How the three edits leave different prefixes to process

summary: Changing book to code illustrates the three remaining prefix subproblems for insertion, deletion, and replacement when the final characters k and e differ.
